topic: False memories: reconsolidation, leading words, planted memories, flashbulb confidence
hook: Your memories change every time you recall them
caption:
Your memories are not recordings. Every time you recall one, your brain rebuilds it and can save it back with small changes. In one classic study, a single word, 'smashed' instead of 'hit', made people remember broken glass that was never there.

This is not just a lab curiosity. According to the Innocence Project, eyewitness misidentification played a role in about 69% of US wrongful convictions later overturned by DNA evidence. (Sources: Loftus & Palmer 1974, Loftus & Pickrell 1995, Talarico & Rubin 2003)

What's one memory you're 100% sure about, but now you're not so sure?

1/5 Recall rewrites it
Each time you remember something, your brain rebuilds the memory and can store it back slightly changed.
🎨 AI-generated image

2/5 One word changes it (1974)
People asked how fast cars 'smashed' into each other guessed higher speeds than those asked how fast they 'hit'.
📷 Shuets Udono (CC BY-SA 2.0) via wikimedia

3/5 Glass that never was (32%)
A week later, 32% of the 'smashed' group remembered broken glass. The crash film showed none.
📷 Sudzie (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

4/5 Planted memories (1 in 4)
In a 1995 study, about 1 in 4 adults came to remember being lost in a mall as kids. It never happened.
📷 WikiPediaAid (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

5/5 Confidence lies too
After 9/11, people's memories of that day drifted like ordinary memories, yet they stayed just as sure they were right.
